text:
The note's claim that patients can always remove adhesive strips themselves is too broad: while many can, proper technique (slow low-angle peeling, supporting skin, gentle solvent for residue) matters, and clinician help is warranted for sensitive areas, fragile skin, or signs of irritation/infection. I'd revise the note to include brief self-removal instructions and a caveat to seek clinician help if the strip is adherent, the skin is damaged, or irritation occurs.  
CONFIDENCE: 75
